facts.statement: The species was described in 1991 based on subfossil material collected in 1976 by Storrs Olson from the Makawehi dunes on Kauai.
facts.quote: It was described in 1991 from subfossil material collected in 1976 by Storrs Olson from the calcareous Makawehi dunes on the south-eastern coast of the island of Kauai.

facts.statement: This species evolved in the Hawaiian Islands located in the North Pacific Ocean.
facts.quote: which evolved in the Hawaiian Islands of the North Pacific Ocean.

facts.statement: Remains of this animal have also been discovered at the nearby Makauwahi Cave site.
facts.quote: Its remains have also been found at the nearby Makauwahi Cave site.

facts.statement: The genus Chelychelynechen contains only this single species.
facts.quote: It is monotypic in the genus Chelychelynechen.

facts.statement: The genus name refers to the bird's distinctly turtle-like beak structure.
facts.quote: The generic name Chelychelynechen comes from the Greek chelys ("turtle"), chelyne ("lip" or "jaw"), with chen ("goose"), referring to the distinctly turtle-like appearance and structure of the beak.

facts.statement: The beak structure suggests the bird adapted to a plant-based diet, showing convergence with tortoises.
facts.quote: The structure of this feeding apparatus appears convergent on that of tortoises and indicates adaptation to a diet of plants.

facts.statement: Apart from its head, the bird possessed robust legs and reduced, non-functional wings similar to other moa-nalo species.
facts.quote: Apart from the head, the bird was similar to other moa-nalo species, with robust legs and reduced, non-functional wings.

facts.statement: The species belongs to the family Anatidae.
